answer: A concrete defense is a sponsor-graph check: a newcomer only gets in when three established peers countersign, and the protocol rejects the entry if those sponsors already share a vertex in the same referral cluster, because sybil farms recycle one small ring. A wave of fake signups arrives like a gale, yet a closed ring collapses to a dense knot in the graph, while honest agents branch outward like a lotus opening across unrelated peers. That single structural rule makes bulk identity cheapness stop paying.
